ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It sets how the re-review runs.
ACTION: Read `fetch/retry.py` around line 41. I need to confirm F1 against the code first: is `attempt` 0-based or 1-based, and what does `max_retries` count?
ACTION: Read `tests/test_retry.py` to see how the existing retry test sets up the fetch.
ACTION: Edit `tests/test_retry.py`. Add a test where every fetch times out, and assert the total call count is exactly 1 + `max_retries`. Run it and confirm it fails (red).
ACTION: Edit `fetch/retry.py:41`. Change `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries`.
ACTION: Run `tests/test_retry.py` and the project's test suite. Confirm the new test and all others pass (green).
ACTION: Commit the fix. Run `<this-skill-dir>/scripts/review-package specs/plans/14-buoy-sync.md <pre-fix HEAD> <fix HEAD>` to write the fix diff file.
ACTION: Dispatch a scoped re-review on `sonnet`, using `re-review-prompt.md`. The prompt names the diff file path and F1 as the only finding. The reviewer returns ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED for F1 and says whether it sees any new Critical or Important issue. This is a small mechanical diff, so `sonnet` is enough.
ACTION: If the re-review is clean, append `Task 4: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, review clean)` to `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/progress.md`. Then dispatch Task 5.

Message to partner:

F1 is a one-character fix, so I will make it myself, as you asked. First I will check the finding against `fetch/retry.py:41`. If the code shows the reviewer is wrong, I will say so and leave it as it is.

I will also add one test that pins the exact retry count. The current test passes with either bound, so it cannot catch this bug.

After the fix, I will run the tests. Then I will send the change to a scoped re-review. You did not ask me to skip the re-review, so Task 4 stays open until it passes.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A test that asserts only "a retry happens" passes for any limit of 1 or more. It cannot tell `>` from `>=`.
- To test a loop bound, make every call fail and count the calls. The count must equal the first try plus the configured retries.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
